neighbours.label: the second person's possessive in a paired-person phrase about spouses or partners (you and your spouse, his or her spouse)
fire: If both you and your spouse work, you may each open a retirement account.
A taxpayer is treated as owning any shares held by his or her spouse.
You and your partner should review the policy together before signing.
Each employee may enroll himself or herself and his or her dependents.
When you and your husband file jointly, the deduction doubles.
The account holder must list his or her beneficiaries on the form.
Both you and your wife will need to sign the mortgage papers.
A member may transfer his or her shares to a family trust.
quiet: If you work full time, you may open a retirement account.
A taxpayer is treated as owning any shares held by a trust.
The partner should review the policy carefully before signing.
Each employee may enroll in the plan during open season.
When married couples file jointly, the deduction doubles.
The account holder must list the beneficiaries on the form.
Both applicants will need to sign the mortgage papers.
A member may transfer shares to a family trust.

short: you and your / his or her
